messages.author: ec83189d181fdaa6
messages.subject: tidyverse and camtrapR compatibility
parts:
Dear all,
in a recent thread, Ayesha and David started a discussion about the compatibility of camtrapR with the tidyverse world. Is that be relevant for many users? And what exactly would you wish for in terms of compatibility?

Here's an idea for how to make camtrapR compatible with tidyverse. It would require a lot of rewriting to make the functions of camtrapR utilize tibbles directly, so I believe the simplest option for now would be to detect if the user provides a tibble as input and if so, automatically convert it to a data frame internally for processing them in camtrapR. Then, if the input was a tibble, the output data frame can also be converted to a tibble automatically. 
Would it be sufficient for your compatibility needs?

My feeling so far is that it would be helpful and I can try to look into it when I have some time. But I'd love to hear your thoughts about this issue first.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.author: 9c3183af58028473
messages.subject: Re: tidyverse and camtrapR compatibility
parts:
Jürgen
I recall I had a lot of grief because when I first brought the excel version of my recordTable into camtrapR as a "tible", not realising that this was not a simple base R data frame.  Ayesha had the same experience.

So my request is - can camtrapR detect when it is being given a "tible" and give a more explicate and earlier warning that camtrapR use base R data frames?
and/or,
can the (excellent) vignette explain that if you are importing a recordTable you must use the class data frame only; read.csv NOT read_xl or read_csv

I am emphatically not suggesting camtrapR be modified to use 'tible' and tidy verse. One of the strengths of camtrapR is that the vignette is so good that an R-beginner can use camtrapR and R.  But a lot of the R learning materials lead one to tidyverse  and that is not helpful with camtrapR.

David

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: tidyverse and camtrapR compatibility
parts:
Hi Patrick,
what exactly do you miss in your workflow, how would you like to go about detection histories for multiple species? 
Since version 1.2 camtrapR can use tibbles (and data.tables) as input and will internally convert them to data.frames. That is for all functions that require input data frames, including detectionHistory(). 

To get detection histories for mutliple species at once, you could: 
- loop over all unique species names in the record table, create detectionHistory for each species (argument species in detectionHistory) and save as list item, OR
- or use lapply() for the same purpose

The resulting list would need to be named with the species names.
Would that be enough? Let me know if that is unclear.
Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.author: 4ae6a6cfae3f0c68
messages.subject: Re: tidyverse and camtrapR compatibility
parts:
I managed to use lapply and things seem to be working great! For anyone else that might be doing something similar the code below is what worked for me! 


##Split recordTable by species 
records.split <- split(records_filter_30min, records_filter_30min$species)




##Build a function for applying to all species
det.hist.apply <- function(x){
  detectionHistory(recordTable = x,
                   species = unique(x$species),
                   camOp                 = camop_problem3, ##Camera operation matrix
                   stationCol            = "Sampling.Unit.Name",
                   speciesCol            = "species",
                   output                = "count",
                   recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",
                   recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                   occasionLength        = 7,
                   day1                  = "survey",
                   datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                   includeEffort         = FALSE,
                   scaleEffort          = FALSE,
  )
}



##Apply the detection history function above to all individual dataframes that are part of the list of species
community.detection.history <- lapply(records.split, det.hist.apply)
